thread:
alex: FYI ran a short apples-to-apples between streaming and non-streaming with the newest kernel-selector heuristics. saw weird tail latency spikes in streaming when KV hit-rate < 30% :thinking_face:

morgan: can you paste the exact harness commands you used? might be config drift vs previous runs.

alex: sure — single-node replay harness, 1k RPS load, mixed seq lengths (16/64/512 distribution). command: ```./bench/replay --workload=prod-sample --rps=1000 --clients=50 --exp-id=client-pacing-2026-03-12```
alex: key thing: streaming path used chunk size=64, readloop backoff=adaptive (window=8->2ms), non-streaming used batch=128, no streaming readloop.
sam: did you pin the same kernel set for both? selector sometimes flips between fast24/fast16 based on observed seq len, which can cause extra memcpy costs during switchover.
alex: yes i pinned model version but left selector policies default. observed selector churn correlated with KV misses. when cache cold, selector changed mid-request for ~2% of streams.
jen: hmm that's interesting — selector churn mid-request should be impossible, probably race in our decision path. can you attach perf traces (p95/p99 token latency per-request) and a flame?
alex: attached small snip of p99 deltas from perf-bot: "streaming p99 = 188ms (tail spikes up to 430ms), non-streaming p99 = 145ms (stable)". also saw CPU sys jitter during thrash.
perf-bot: experiment client-pacing-2026-03-12 completed. artifacts: s3://redwood-perf/client-pacing-2026-03-12/{trace.json, kernel-log.txt, kv-stats.csv}
morgan: can we reproduce with a synthetic harness that controls KV hit-rate explicitly? replay has too much variability from real traces.
sam: yes, create a synthetic generator that emits the same token distributions but injects a deterministic KV miss ratio (0%, 10%, 30%, 60%). then run both streaming and non-streaming with identical kernel pins.
alex: ran quick loop for 0% vs 40% misses: streaming lost advantage once misses >20%. hypothesis: streaming amortizes kernel switch cost across chunks, but when chunks are small plus miss-induced mem copies, overhead dominates.
nate: idea: make selector use a per-request stable decision based on first-chunk statistics (avoid reselect mid-request). fallback path can still adapt between requests. keeps low risk but reduces churn.
jen: agreed. low-risk change: sticky-selector=true for streaming experiments, plus add metric: selector_reselect_count per-request.
morgan: also change readloop pacing to prefer slightly larger chunk when KV hit-rate low (so fewer selector decisions). we can try chunk=96 for streaming as A/B.
sam: note: changing chunk size impacts prefix-cache reuse and latency SLO. make sure we run quality evals.
alex: next steps I propose:
- implement sticky-selector toggle on runtime (flag: --sticky-selector)
- add synthetic harness that can set KV miss ratio explicitly (script: perf/synth_kv_driver.py)
- run matrix: {streaming,non-streaming} x {miss=0,10,30,60} x {chunk=64,96,128} x 3 seeds
- capture selector_reselect_count, p50/p95/p99 token latency, cpu_sys, and cache_hit_rate

will start PR for sticky-selector and upload harness tonight. tagging @morgan @sam for review.

morgan: thanks — can you also include a short doc blurb in the run artifact that lists exact kernel pinning and runtime flags? makes future apples-to-apples easier.
alex: yep will do. I'll also add a small note about how replay vs synthetic differed for this experiment in case folks run follow-ups.
jen: if we see mid-request selector still happening after sticky change, escalate to kernel selection owners (assign to @sam).
sam: ack. if we need a deeper dive i'll add sampling PMUs on the node for next run.
nate: one more: for reporting, include per-token breakdown for first 32 tokens vs rest. streaming tends to pay more per-token at the beginning when cache cold.
alex: good call. ok starting runs now, will post results thread when done. :rocket:
